disorder.name: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders

stage1_hpo_curation.extraction_prompt_addendum: DSM-5-TR Schizophrenia Criterion A is polythetic (2 or more of five distinct symptoms; at least one from A.1, A.2, A.3). Route each to its OWN domain: A.1 delusions -> delusions; A.2 hallucinations -> hallucinations; A.3 disorganized speech / formal thought disorder -> disorganized_speech; A.4 behavior that is grossly disorganized or catatonic -> catatonic_disorganized_behavior (bidirectional: immobility AND excessive purposeless activity, emit two items); A.5 negative symptoms -> negative_symptoms (emit diminished emotional expression and avolition as separate items). Do NOT map any symptom to a salience or PPI substrate: the aberrant-salience endophenotype is the mechanism axis, populated on the mouse side, NOT a face-valid analog of the phenomenology. Do NOT emit cognitive-executive or generic-social items as SCZ criteria (those are DSM associated features, not Criterion A) -> other. Extract phenotype FEATURES as short normalized phrases. Delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized speech have no direct mouse analog; that unmodellability is the result and is captured by those domains scoring near zero.

stage2_rerank.developer_prompt_addendum: The 5 SCZ DSM-5-TR Criterion A domains: delusions, hallucinations, disorganized_speech, disorganized_catatonic_behavior, negative_symptoms. Mouse-proxy guidance: (a) positive symptoms (A.1-A.3) lack direct mouse correlates; established operational proxies include prepulse-inhibition (PPI) deficits → direct_analog for sensorimotor-gating dimension of A.1/A.2/A.3, enhanced locomotor/behavioral response to MK-801/PCP/amphetamine → direct_analog for psychotomimetic-response dimension, working-memory deficits → close_support for A.3 disorganized cognition; (b) negative symptoms (A.5): decreased social interaction → close_support for avolition (note: also maps to ASD — disambiguate via downstream disorder-specific gene evidence), anhedonia behaviors → close_support (overlaps with MDD); (c) catatonic behavior (A.4) is BIDIRECTIONAL: motor stereotypy / catalepsy / immobility → direct_analog for catatonic-immobility direction, hyperlocomotion / frenetic activity → direct_analog for catatonic-agitation direction; treat opposite-direction phenotypes that map to the SISTER directional target on the same axis as NOT mismatch (sister-target evidence); (d) ultrasonic vocalization abnormalities → weak_support for A.3 disorganized speech (USV abnormalities are also common in ASD — disambiguation comes downstream). strict_eligible=true only for high-quality organism-level analogs suitable for strict SCZ-domain support.

score_floor.provenance: 0.57 was derived for ASD broad_v3 (2026-05-09 lab notebook): balanced-accuracy maximization of transparent_score against the LLM's own broad_eligible verdicts on the 180 LLM-judged pairs inside ambiguous-target rerank bundles. At θ=0.57, BA=0.736, precision=0.83, recall=0.70. Note: the 180 pairs were LLM-judged, not hand-curated — θ is a score-self-consistency threshold, not an externally-validated behavioral-analog cutoff.
score_floor.applies_to: Stage 2c fill pass. Pairs with transparent_score >= 0.57 that Stage 2b did not bundle (because their target was non-ambiguous or they sat below top-N) are submitted to the LLM for a second-pass eligibility judgment with the identical prompt and schema. Does NOT filter Stage 2b LLM-strict-eligible pairs (those bypass the floor).
score_floor.per_disorder_tuning_policy: DISALLOWED. Per-disorder θ tuning would add 20 DOF that reviewers see as fishing (Mode C), and the per-disorder calibration set would be each disorder's LLM verdicts — circular (Mode D, since we are gating Stage 2c LLM calls against Stage 2b LLM labels). If a future contributor needs per-disorder floor behavior, switch from a tuned VALUE to a uniform RULE (e.g., 80th-percentile of pair scores per disorder), so the same logic applies automatically across all disorders without per-disorder choices.
score_floor.scz_specific_diagnostic_2026_05_27: BA-max recalibration was performed on the 185 SCZ-specific LLM verdicts as a diagnostic (NOT applied): SCZ optimum θ=0.63 (BA=0.661, P=0.825, R=0.448). The BA-max degradation from 0.736 (ASD) to 0.661 (SCZ) reflects weaker score↔LLM-verdict alignment for SCZ, a consequence of higher structural_missing rate (97% of SCZ pairs lack ontology channels). Per the universal-value policy, this disorder-specific θ was NOT adopted. See scz_pair_rerank_v1/_ba_max_sweep_broad.tsv for the full sweep.

sensitivity_sweep_plan.outputs: rerun Stage 2c -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 once per floor; report AUROC across A2 (headline) and A1 (psychiatric pool); flag if any headline AUROC moves > 0.02 across the range.
sensitivity_sweep_plan.rationale: Pre-register the sweep before observing T0 AUROC so the robustness claim is blinded to outcome, not post-hoc.

stage2_rerank._top_n_bundle_rationale: Reverted from 10 to 5 (2026-05-27) so the lexical-downweight sensitivity test isolates the effect of the new factor cleanly. If lexical-downweight alone surfaces the catatonia↔catalepsy match at top_n=5, the wider bundle was a workaround for the wrong underlying problem.
stage2_rerank._lexical_downweight_rationale: Lexical channel was originally introduced as a guard against LLM/semantic over-reach in ontology mapping (no established protocol for using LLMs in ontology research at design time). When both Resnik IC AND Jaccard channels are absent (structural_missing=True), the redistribution math inflates lexical's effective contribution from its 25%% baseline to ~35.7%% — exactly when lexical's guard role is also least defensible because there is no ontology channel left to validate either signal. Setting factor=0.5 halves lexical's weight in that case (effective ~22%% vs original 25%%), letting embed dominate (~78%%) for cross-jargon semantic matches like Catalepsy↔Catatonia where token overlap is zero but semantic similarity is high. Validated by parity test on ASD: if ASD headline AUROC is stable (most ASD pairs have IC/Jaccard present, factor doesn't fire), the change is defensible to apply across disorders. Test date 2026-05-27.

stage3_aggregation.polarity_deferral_note: SCZ polarity considerations: positive symptoms (A.1-A.3) are unidirectional (presence of abnormality); negative symptoms (A.5) are also unidirectional (absence/deficit is itself the abnormality); A.4 catatonic behavior is the only intrinsically BIDIRECTIONAL domain (motor immobility OR excessive activity). v1 uses polarity-off; v2 may add an SCZ-specific polarity schema with catatonia-aware bidirectional handling.

stage5_benchmark._b_family_comparator_2026_05_27: B1-B4 use comparator_pool_ids = [A1, A5] (union of psychiatric pool and ASD_primary). The Stage 5 driver resolves the union and passes it to domain_hypothesis_tests.py via --negative_groups. This is the powered comparator for SCZ Tier 0 (n~211); A2 would over-dilute.
stage5_benchmark._n_mp_thresholds_2026_05_27: Depth-bias sweep added per §6g audit (LAB_NOTEBOOK_ENTRY_2026-05-27). Top-100 Phenodigm-ranked mice have median n_mp_terms=1 (q90=3); they score high because their single high-IC MP term dominates the asymmetric BMA mean. Stage 4's permutation null is the depth-stratified correction the new pipeline applies; Phenodigm does not. To make the cross-method comparison interpretable, AUROC is reported restricted to genotypes with n_mp_terms >= K for K in {1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 10}. Primary headline threshold is n_mp >= 4 (excludes ~96% of Phenodigm artifact-zone mice while preserving 77% of SCZ_primary positives, 86% of ASD_primary). n_mp >= 5 is a more aggressive alternative primary (98% artifact exclusion, 65% SCZ_primary retention) reported as robustness check. The n_mp filter is applied at AUROC-compute time inside compute_benchmark_metrics.py + compare_methods_paired.py against BOTH the new pipeline and the Phenodigm baseline — Phenodigm scores do NOT need re-running.
stage5_benchmark.outdir_template_change_2026_07_28: Each disorder carried its own stale dated stamp: ASD 2026-05-11, SCZ 2026-05-28, ID 2026-06-02, NCD 2026-07-27. strict.name: delusions
strict.description: DSM-5-TR SCZ Criterion A.1: delusions, firmly held false beliefs that do not shift when evidence runs against them (persecutory, referential, grandiose, thought insertion/withdrawal/broadcasting).

strict.name: hallucinations
strict.description: DSM-5-TR SCZ Criterion A.2: hallucinations, perception-like experiences without an external stimulus (auditory most common).

strict.name: disorganized_speech
strict.description: DSM-5-TR SCZ Criterion A.3: disorganized speech, derailment, incoherence, tangentiality, word salad.

strict.name: catatonic_disorganized_behavior
strict.description: DSM-5-TR SCZ Criterion A.4: behavior that is grossly disorganized or catatonic, from childlike silliness to agitation that cannot be predicted, and catatonia (immobility, waxy flexibility, mutism, stupor, negativism, posturing, OR excessive purposeless motor activity). PARTIALLY MODELLABLE and the most tractable positive-pole criterion: catatonia has organism-level mouse analogs. Bidirectional (immobility AND excessive activity). Mouse anchors: catalepsy / bar test, waxy flexibility, immobility, locomotor disorganization.

strict.name: negative_symptoms
strict.description: DSM-5-TR SCZ Criterion A.5: negative symptoms, diminished emotional expression (reduced affect, prosody, gesture) and avolition (reduced motivated goal-directed activity); includes alogia, anhedonia, asociality. MOST MODELLABLE of Criterion A. Mouse anchors: reduced affect proxies, progressive-ratio break point and effort-based decision tasks (avolition), sucrose preference (anhedonia), reduced social engagement (asociality). Emit diminished-expression and avolition as separate items.

scored_criterionA_domains.salience_dysregulation: DSM-5 A1 delusions + A2 hallucinations. No mouse behavioral analog -> scores ~0 across all genotypes and the background pool. KEPT and reported as un-mappable (FACET deliverable).
scored_criterionA_domains.disorganization: DSM-5 A3 disorganized speech (un-mappable, ~0) + A4 grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior (MAPPABLE via catatonia/catalepsy/disorganized behavior). Carries signal from A4.
scored_criterionA_domains.negative_symptoms_motivation: DSM-5 A5 negative symptoms (diminished emotional expression, avolition). MAPPABLE via social withdrawal, anhedonia, avolition.

excluded_not_criterionA.cognitive_executive: NOT a DSM-5 Criterion A symptom; DSM lists cognitive impairment as an associated feature, explicitly non-diagnostic. Was the largest contributor (0.0452) -> the baseless part of the prior 0.866.
excluded_not_criterionA.social_interaction: DSM-5 Criterion B (functional decline: work/interpersonal/self-care), not a Criterion A symptom. 2/3 of its terms are B (social/occupational deterioration, impairment in personality functioning). The 1 A5-asociality term (Diminishment of social interactions) belongs conceptually with negative_symptoms_motivation.

_dsm_realignment_2026-07-23.note: Full DSM-5 Criterion A set is scored, including un-mappable A1/A2/A3 (scored 0, reported). Non-criterion domains (cognitive_executive, social_interaction/Crit B) excluded. Asociality term optionally foldable into A5 via a term re-domain if desired.
_dsm_realignment_2026-07-23.aggregator: mean over the 3 Criterion A domains (macro-average)

mechanism_axis.name: salience_dysregulation_endophenotype
mechanism_axis.reported: separately from face validity; NOT in domains.strict and NOT in the discrimination composite
mechanism_axis.content: aberrant-salience endophenotype substrate: prepulse inhibition, sensorimotor gating, latent inhibition, dopamine-mediated psychotomimetic hyper-response, amphetamine and NMDA-antagonist sensitivity
mechanism_axis.rationale: endophenotype substrate of the positive-symptom pole; not a DSM-5 diagnostic criterion; the dimension SCZ mouse models actually capture and that the Phenodigm baseline rewards (endophenotype-attribution probe 2026-07-27: PPI + sensorimotor gating carry the majority of Phenodigm's SCZ best-matches)
mechanism_axis.measurement: the Phenodigm-contrast / endophenotype-attribution probe, reported as the mechanism axis distinct from criterion face validity
